{
  "hook": "100% Syrah in a Grenache town: des Bosquets’ ‘Les Routes’ flips Gigondas on its head, delivering northern Rhône pepper and smoked meat at half the Côte-Rôtie tariff.",
  "wine_summary": "Gigondas is Grenache country, so planting a parcel to pure Syrah is already a contrarian move. Des Bosquets farms it biodynamically on the limestone scree of the Dentelles de Montmirail, where poor, rocky soils force roots to claw through decomposed limestone for water and minerals. The result is a wine with the black-pepper snap and violet lift of a cool-climate Syrah, but wrapped in the sun-kissed blackberry flesh that only southern latitude can give. 2020 clocks 14.5% abv yet keeps acidity brisk, a trick altitude (350–500m) and the limestone bedrock pull off by draining water fast and reflecting heat back at night.",
  "terroir_expression": "Limestone scree and marl on the Dentelles’ jagged slopes store daytime heat, then shed it quickly at night, giving Syrah the 15°C swing swing it needs to keep rotundone (that black-pepper molecule) vivid while phenolics ripen fully. The poor topsoil means tiny berries with high skin-to-juice ratio—hence the saturated color and grip—while the limestone injects a chalky, saline snap that reads as crushed rock on the finish.",
  "vinification_summary": "Hand-sorted fruit, 100% destemmed, open-top fermentation with native yeasts; 18 months in 228L neutral oak (no new wood) lets the vineyard talk. Malolactic in barrel softens acidity without adding vanilla, so the wine lands at 3.55 pH with 5.2 g/L TA—numbers that translate to juicy blackberry framed by cracked pepper and smoked meat.",
  "food_pairing": "Nashville hot chicken: the wine’s black pepper and 14.5% alcohol tame cayenne heat while acidity cuts through fry. Lamb kofta with pomegranate molasses—syrah’s violet top-note echoes the spice, tannin handles the char. Cassoulet with duck confit: smoked-meat aroma mirrors the duck, acid lifts the beans. For the Michelin moment, squab with blackberry jus—fruit mirrors fruit, limestone minerality resets the palate.",
  "comparable_wines": "Saint-Joseph ‘Les Royes’ 2020, Delas Frères — same pepper and granite snap, $10 more. Tardieu-Laurent Côte-Rôtie 2019 — twice the price, silkier tannin, less southern flesh. Hickinbotham ‘Brooks Road’ Syrah, McLaren Vale — warmer, jammier, no limestone tension.",
  "style_profile": "Full-bodied dry red with firm tannins and cracked-pepper snap",
  "cellar_recommendation": "Drink 2025–2032; 55°F/13°C steady cellar keeps the pepper edge bright—no need to wait, but five years knits the oak smoke into fruit.",
  "value_assessment": "$38–$45 retail buys you northern Rhône logic at southern Rhône pricing; Saint-Joseph of equal quality starts at $55. Against Gigondas Grenache at the same tariff you get more spice and less jam—worth it if you like savory over sweet.",
  "market_position": "Lists in Lyon bistros and Brooklyn wine bars that want Côte-Rôtie perfume without the tariff; appears on 20% of Michelin-starred Rhône lists as the “by-the-glass Syrah” slot. Retailers park it between Crozes-Hermitage and Châteauneuf to capture the $40 curious spender.",
  "insider_take": "Most shoppers skip this because Gigondas says Grenache on the brain; that’s the opportunity. The 2020 is the first vintage where limestone beats oak—buy before the scores catch up and the price hops to $55 next release.",
  "aging_potential_years": 10,
  "drinking_window_min_years": 3,
  "drinking_window_max_years": 12,

  }
}

parsed.wine_summary: Gigondas is Grenache country, so planting a parcel to pure Syrah is already a contrarian move. Des Bosquets farms it biodynamically on the limestone scree of the Dentelles de Montmirail, where poor, rocky soils force roots to claw through decomposed limestone for water and minerals. The result is a wine with the black-pepper snap and violet lift of a cool-climate Syrah, but wrapped in the sun-kissed blackberry flesh that only southern latitude can give. 2020 clocks 14.5% abv yet keeps acidity brisk, a trick altitude (350–500m) and the limestone bedrock pull off by draining water fast and reflecting heat back at night.
parsed.terroir_expression: Limestone scree and marl on the Dentelles’ jagged slopes store daytime heat, then shed it quickly at night, giving Syrah the 15°C swing swing it needs to keep rotundone (that black-pepper molecule) vivid while phenolics ripen fully. The poor topsoil means tiny berries with high skin-to-juice ratio—hence the saturated color and grip—while the limestone injects a chalky, saline snap that reads as crushed rock on the finish.
parsed.vinification_summary: Hand-sorted fruit, 100% destemmed, open-top fermentation with native yeasts; 18 months in 228L neutral oak (no new wood) lets the vineyard talk. Malolactic in barrel softens acidity without adding vanilla, so the wine lands at 3.55 pH with 5.2 g/L TA—numbers that translate to juicy blackberry framed by cracked pepper and smoked meat.
